title: Mobile test — Dealer Locator at 360x600
featureSummary: Verify the dealer locator page (https://www.michelinman.com/auto/dealer-locator) renders and behaves correctly on a 360x600 mobile viewport: search input visibility/overflow, the deferred 'Locate me' control, the top-cities horizontal scroller, city selection reaching the results page, and the total number of top cities offered.
conclusion: 1 CRITICAL AC failure (only 5 top cities, AC-4 requires more than 5) and 1 MAJOR accessibility gap (the 'Locate me' control cannot be reached by keyboard even after becoming visible) block approval. AC-1, AC-2 and AC-3 pass on their own merits.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: The dealer search input is fully visible and tappable at 360px width, with no horizontal overflow on the page. The "Locate me" control may be hidden until the search input is focused, but must become fully visible once focus occurs.

The top cities horizontal scroller is swipeable on mobile, and every city (Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New-York) can be scrolled into view and tapped — the fade gradient on the scroller's edges must not visually cover or block taps on the last visible city.
Selecting a city from mobile reaches the results page, and dealer cards stack in a single readable column with no text truncation or overlapping elements.
Dealer search page should have more than 5 cities.

commentScenarios.summary: Once the "Locate me" control becomes visible after focusing the search input, can it actually be reached and activated using only the keyboard (Tab, then Enter) — not just a mouse or touch tap?
commentScenarios.notes: No — pressing Tab from the focused search input skips straight to the first top-city link (Atlanta). The Locate me button keeps tabIndex=-1 even though its opacity goes 0→1 on focus, so it can never receive keyboard focus and Enter can never be pressed on it. Reproduced identically in the main run and in a fresh second context. See BUG-1.

scenarios.name: Sanity — dealer locator page loads at 360x600 with its core elements
steps: Navigate to https://www.michelinman.com/auto/dealer-locator at 360x600
Dismiss the consent banner
Verify the search input and top-cities list render
Check the console for errors
scenarios.expected: Page loads with the search input, Locate me control and top-cities list present; no console errors.
scenarios.actual: Page loaded correctly with all core elements present, but a CSP violation (blocked data:audio/mpeg resource) and a 400 on a first-party status-log endpoint fire on every load, unrelated to any test action — see BUG-3 (MINOR).

scenarios.name: AC-1 — search input fully visible/tappable, no horizontal page overflow
steps: Measure the search input's bounding box (x:16, width:328) against the 360px viewport
Measure document.documentElement.scrollWidth vs clientWidth
scenarios.expected: Input sits fully within the 360px viewport; scrollWidth equals clientWidth (no horizontal overflow).
scenarios.actual: Input box is x:16→344 of 360px, fully on-screen. scrollWidth (360) === clientWidth (360). No horizontal overflow.

scenarios.name: AC-1 — Locate me hidden pre-focus, fully visible once search input is focused
steps: Read Locate me's opacity/tabIndex/width before focus
Click (focus) the search input
Re-read Locate me's opacity/tabIndex/width after focus
scenarios.expected: Locate me may be invisible pre-focus, but must become fully visible on focus.
scenarios.actual: Pre-focus: opacity 0, width 18px (effectively invisible/off-canvas). Post-focus: opacity 1, width 312px, fully within the viewport — AC-1's visibility requirement is met.

scenarios.name: Comment scenario — Locate me keyboard reachability (Tab, Enter) once visible
steps: Focus the search input
Press Tab once
Read document.activeElement
Read Locate me's tabIndex
scenarios.expected: Focus should be able to reach the now-visible Locate me control via Tab, so Enter can activate it.
scenarios.actual: Focus skips Locate me entirely and lands on the "Atlanta" top-city link. Locate me's tabIndex remains -1 even after opacity becomes 1. Enter can never be pressed on an element that never receives focus. Reproduced identically in a fresh second context.

scenarios.name: AC-2 — top-cities scroller is horizontally scrollable and edge gradients don't block taps
steps: Inspect .dl__top-cities-list: overflow-x, touch-action, scrollWidth vs clientWidth
Inspect the left/right fade-gradient elements: pointer-events, z-index
Scroll the list to its maximum scrollLeft and hit-test each visible city link with elementFromPoint
scenarios.expected: The list is genuinely scrollable and the fade gradients never intercept a tap on the city underneath them.
scenarios.actual: overflow-x:auto, touch-action:auto, scrollWidth 550 vs clientWidth 328 — mechanically scrollable. Both gradients have pointer-events:none, z-index:1. After scrolling to the end, elementFromPoint at Dallas/Los Angeles/New-York's on-screen centers all resolved inside their own anchor (isAnchorOrChild:true) — the gradients never intercept the tap.

scenarios.name: AC-2 — New-York (last city) can be scrolled into view and tapped, navigates correctly
steps: Scroll .dl__top-cities-list to its end
Click the New-York link
Verify the resulting URL
scenarios.expected: Clicking New-York navigates to its dealer results page.
scenarios.actual: Native click on the scrolled-into-view New-York link navigated to https://www.michelinman.com/auto/dealer-locator/new-york.

scenarios.name: AC-3 — dealer results page stacks cards in a single column, no truncation or overlap at 360px
steps: Land on /auto/dealer-locator/new-york
Measure each card's bounding box and address text scrollWidth vs clientWidth
Check for vertical overlap between consecutive cards
scenarios.expected: Single-column card layout, address text not truncated, no overlap.
scenarios.actual: 20 cards loaded, all width 328 / x:16 (single column). Address text scrollWidth === clientWidth for every sampled card (not truncated). No overlaps detected between consecutive cards. document scrollWidth (360) === clientWidth (360), no page-level horizontal overflow either.

scenarios.name: AC-4 — dealer search page should have more than 5 cities
steps: Count anchors inside .dl__top-cities-list
Repeat the count in a fresh browser context
scenarios.expected: More than 5 top cities are offered.
scenarios.actual: Exactly 5 cities are offered (Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New-York) — no more, no less. Confirmed identically in the main run and in a fresh second context. See BUG-2.

scenarios.name: Boundary — back button after viewing results restores the search page
steps: From /auto/dealer-locator/new-york, press browser Back
Verify the search input and top-cities list are present again
scenarios.expected: Back button returns to a working search page.
scenarios.actual: Back navigation returned to https://www.michelinman.com/auto/dealer-locator with the search input and top-cities list both present.

scenarios.name: Boundary — URL persistence: a results URL opened directly in a fresh tab loads correctly
steps: Open a fresh page and navigate directly to /auto/dealer-locator/atlanta
Count dealer cards
scenarios.expected: Deep-linking straight to a results URL works without going through the search flow.
scenarios.actual: Fresh tab navigated directly to the Atlanta results URL and rendered 20 dealer cards.

scenarios.name: Boundary — rapid repeated clicks on a top-city link do not crash or get stuck
steps: Click the Chicago top-city link 5 times in rapid succession
scenarios.expected: A single correct navigation occurs; no crash, no stuck intermediate state.
scenarios.actual: First click navigated to /auto/dealer-locator/chicago; subsequent click attempts against the now-stale locator simply timed out (expected Playwright behaviour once the element has navigated away) — no crash, no stuck UI.

scenarios.name: TC-AN1 — analytics fires on interaction
steps: Snapshot window.dataLayer length and attach a request listener before the first interaction
Focus the search input, navigate between cities and the results page
Re-check dataLayer length and captured requests
scenarios.expected: At least one analytics request or dataLayer push after interaction.
scenarios.actual: 39 analytics-endpoint requests captured (incl. googletagmanager.com/gtm.js) and window.dataLayer grew from 16 to 18 entries.

bugs.title: "Locate me" control is unreachable by keyboard even after it becomes visible on focus
steps: Focus the search input (click or Tab into it)
Observe Locate me's opacity go from 0 to 1
Press Tab once
bugs.expected: Focus moves to the now-visible Locate me button so it can be activated with Enter.
bugs.actual: Focus skips Locate me and lands on the first top-city link (Atlanta). document.querySelector('.dl__autocomplete-locate').tabIndex is -1 both before and after focus/visibility change — the element is permanently removed from the tab order regardless of its visual state. This is a mechanical, self-evident DOM property (not an inferred root cause), reproduced identically in a second fresh browser context.
bugs.impact: Keyboard-only and switch-device users can never activate geolocation search, even though the control is visibly present and mouse/touch users can tap it.

bugs.title: Dealer locator top-cities list has exactly 5 cities; AC-4 requires more than 5
steps: Load the dealer locator page
Count the anchors inside .dl__top-cities-list
bugs.actual: Exactly 5 cities: Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New-York. Count is a literal DOM count, not an inference — reproduced identically in a second fresh browser context.
bugs.impact: AC-4 is not met; there is no workaround short of a content/CMS change to add more cities.

bugs.title: CSP violation blocks a base64 audio resource, plus a 400 on a first-party status-log endpoint, on every page load
steps: Load the page with no test interaction at all
bugs.expected: No console errors on a clean load.
bugs.actual: A Content-Security-Policy violation blocks a data:audio/mpeg resource under default-src *, and a 400 fires on https://dctityd.michelinman.com/status-log. Both fire before any test action, so they are pre-existing/site-wide rather than caused by this test — flagged for developer confirmation rather than treated as a regression from this ticket's change.
bugs.impact: No visible UI impact observed; noise in the console/network panel only.

observations: Native touch-gesture dispatch (Playwright CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent and Input.synthesizeScrollGesture, multiple parameter variations) did not move .dl__top-cities-list's scrollLeft in this automated mobile-emulated context, even though the container is mechanically scrollable (overflow-x:auto, touch-action:auto) and setting scrollLeft programmatically works and clamps correctly at scrollWidth-clientWidth. Treated as an automation-tooling limitation, not a product bug — AC-2's actual requirement (scrollability + un-blocked taps) was verified by the mechanical CSS properties and by elementFromPoint hit-testing after a programmatic scroll, which is the best available substitute evidence given the constraint. Worth a manual real-device swipe check to be fully certain.

When the search input is focused, .dl__autocomplete--wrapper (the suggestions-dropdown container) expands from a 16x17px near-zero box to an absolutely-positioned ~279px-tall box that sits over the area where the top-cities list renders. This only happens while the input is actively focused/has a dropdown open, which is normal autocomplete behaviour, not a bug — but it does mean a user cannot simultaneously have the suggestions panel open and tap a top city; they would need to blur/dismiss the input first. Not raised as a bug because AC-2 does not require simultaneous access.

Dealer card address text was NOT truncated at 360x600 — this differs from an earlier note (recorded at 390x844) where the address span was CSS-truncated with a fixed 300px width. Either the breakpoint behaviour genuinely differs at 360px vs 390px, or the earlier truncation has since been fixed; worth a targeted recheck at 390x844 in a future run to confirm which.

The existing suite's generated feature (features/generated/SCRUM-1.feature) already has a scenario asserting 'I should see at least 5 top cities' — this ticket's AC-4 tightens that to 'more than 5', which the site does not meet. The two scenarios are not in conflict (5 satisfies 'at least 5' but not 'more than 5'), but a future automated regression test for AC-4 should use the stricter 'more than 5' assertion, not reuse the existing 'at least 5' one.

automationGap.recommendation: 'Mobile and tablet viewports' and 'Keyboard navigation and focus visibility' are both already declared as known gaps in features/COVERAGE.md, and this run landed real, reproducible findings in exactly both: AC-4's city count only fails at all because nobody had asserted 'more than 5' (vs the existing 'at least 5'), and the Locate me keyboard trap is a focus-visibility gap of exactly the declared kind. Closing these two — a stricter city-count assertion and a focus-order assertion — would directly retire two named gaps, not just add generic mobile coverage.
